name: A native-backed Closeable object closes idempotently from script

input.source_text: module M { public fun run() -> Object { let r = NativeFixture.resource(); let first = r.close(); let second = r.close(); [first, second, r.releases] } } M.run()

applicability.reason: Supported. C027 validates the payload descriptor BEFORE the runtime owns any storage, so the resource reaches script only once registration succeeded, and C030 makes deterministic release explicit and IDEMPOTENT. The C boundary already proved the property; what was missing is the SCRIPT half this row names. `NativeFixture.resource()` now answers an identity-bearing FFI::Resource whose close goes to the real C ABI, so both calls answer nil and the native release counter reads exactly 1. The counter is read back through the same boundary rather than tracked in the evaluator, which is what makes the idempotence observed rather than asserted.
